reasoning: Vermont has no U.S. Senate or presidential race on the ballot in 2026, and no reputable polls or forecasts in the last 45 days address a current margin for either federal race in the state.[1][7] The most recent structural indicator is the statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index, which rates Vermont as strongly Democratic at about D+16, suggesting that when those races next occur, Democrats would start with a substantial advantage even though no fresh head‑to‑head numbers exist. Given the absence of new race-specific data in the last 45 days, the best available characterization is that Vermont remains heavily D‑leaning, but no current numeric D+ or R+ margin can be responsibly assigned for an active Senate or presidential contest.

sources.name: Cook Political Report
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s statewide Partisan Voting Index places Vermont at roughly D+16, indicating a strongly Democratic lean relative to the national average.

sources.name: Politifinder (compilation of official VT 2024 Senate results)
sources.details: Reports the certified 2024 Vermont U.S. Senate result, with Bernie Sanders defeating Republican Gerald Malloy 61.53% to 31.25%, a Sanders margin of about 30 points, confirming Vermont’s strong Democratic tilt in recent federal Senate voting.

sources.name: Burlington Free Press / UNH Survey Center polling
sources.details: UNH Survey Center polling and coverage on Phil Scott’s approval show weakening support for the Republican governor, reinforcing the broader picture of a Democratic-leaning electorate even though the poll is not about a federal race margin.

sources.name: Prediction Edge Vermont elections overview
sources.details: Explains that no U.S. Senate seat is up in Vermont in 2026 and that the next Senate contest will be in 2028, meaning there is no active 2026 Senate race margin to measure.
